description:
Donald Trump says it's "largely true" that the US-Israel war in Iran was responsible for sweeping Republican losses in the US midterm elections.
 
His comments come after US Vice-President, JD Vance, said in an social media post "the reason we lost is the war."

The President has said he has no plans for immediate strikes on Iran after the vote, but the region remains on alert for any further military action.
 
The BBC's International Editor, Jeremy Bowen - alongside colleagues from the United States and BBC Persian - provides analysis of what the midterm results mean for the war and where things might go from here.

description:
Today, with most of the votes counted in the US midterm elections the Democratic Party has taken control of Congress. 

A string of Republican strongholds turned blue including Texas, South Carolina and Kansas. President Trump earlier acknowledged the that Iran war and the rising cost of living were factors in his party’s defeat.  To assess why the democrats have done so well, and what this means for the next two years of Trump’s presidency, James Cook is joined from Washington by chief news presenter Caitríona Perry and Stephen Hawkins, global director of research at the pollster More in Common.  

And, Chris Mason has been talking to Ed Miliband for Newscast in Antigua. They unpack the implications of the UK Government considering a formal apology for the UK's role in the transatlantic slave trade.

description:
Can a new crop of Democrats in Congress end the war in Iran?

Democrats have taken control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, dealing a major blow to President Donald Trump. The result could have significant implications for US foreign policy – and for the conflicts unfolding overseas.

The Global Story’s Asma Khalid and Tristan Redman explore what the results mean for America’s role in the world. They hear from Democratic Representative Jason Crow and Damian Murphy of the Center for American Progress about how congressional Democrats plan to challenge Trump’s foreign policy agenda – from the wars in Iran and Ukraine to America’s relationships with its allies and adversaries.

description:
The Democrats have won control of the Senate and House of Representatives in the 2026 US midterm elections. The sweeping victory saw Democrats flip seats in conservative strongholds like Texas, Kansas and South Carolina. Democrat Senator Jon Ossoff, who won re-election in Georgia, said Americans had delivered a rebuke of Donald Trump. Vice-President JD Vance has blamed the Iran war for the Republicans' poor showing, saying it was the main reason people abandoned the party. 

In this video, we ask our analyst why voters turned against the president and his party, and whether the Maga movement still has power. Plus, our correspondent in Michigan reports on the historic victory for Abdul El-Sayed, who will become America's first Muslim senator - and how it could point to a new, more progressive direction for the Democrats.

description:
What’s next for the Democrats, and for the last two years of Trump’s presidency? As Democrats make sweeping gains across traditional red states in America, Justin, Anthony and Sarah discuss how it was done, and the impact for Democrats and Donald Trump.

Kansas has elected its first Democratic senator since the 1930s. South Carolina has rejected a Senate candidate strongly endorsed by Donald Trump. And Iowa and Ohio have also gone to the Democrats. Mississippi, meanwhile, is still too close to call. The president has said he will accept the results. But with Democrats in control of Congress, what can he still get done?

Justin, Sarah and Anthony ask what this means for the rest of the Trump presidency, and which way both parties might now turn as they look ahead to 2028.

author: BBC News
description:
The Democrats have won a blowout victory in the US midterm elections, winning the Senate and the House of Representatives, taking control of Congress for the rest of Donald Trump's presidency.
 
In the Senate race, Republican strongholds have been toppled by the Democrats in Texas, Ohio and Kansas, which last elected a Democrat almost 100 years ago.
 
Trump has congratulated the Democrats on a “good job” and acknowledged that gas prices hurt Republicans during the midterm races, saying people "didn't like it" when they had to pay more for fuel.
 
The midterm elections happen mid-way through every 4-year presidential election cycle, giving Americans the chance to elect members of Congress, which is made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate.
 
Here is how the night unfolded.

author: BBC News
description:
Democrat James Talarico has won a key Senate race in Texas, in what is likely the single biggest upset for Republicans in this year's elections.
 
Talarico's stunning victory over Republican Ken Paxton marks the first time a Democrat has won a US Senate seat in Texas since 1988 - and has helped solidify Democrats taking full control of the US Congress in a tidal wave of wins across the US.
 
Paxton sought to portray Talarico's views as too progressive for the state, and campaigned alongside Trump on several occasions.
 
As the nation's second most populous state, Texas has been a bastion of conservatism, routinely rolling out Republican policies that are later employed elsewhere.
